headline: High: Airbyte’s broad egress can move business data into LlamaFactory workflows, creating default data-leakage and compliance risk despite LlamaFactory’s local-only profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Airbyte has broad network egress, but LlamaFactory has no clipboard, files, stdin/stdout, MCP, or browser surfaces, and no evidence shows it ingests Airbyte outputs as instructions. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF LlamaFactory begins parsing Airbyte-produced text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for typed, human-reviewed summaries.
Disable any future shared clipboard or shared workspace integration.
Require explicit provenance labels on any Airbyte output before reuse.
Add a manual review step before LlamaFactory consumes external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress, so it can transmit sensitive business data outward by default. LlamaFactory is documented as local-only on the provided profile, with no filesystem read or network egress, so the leakage path is one-way and less severe than a third-party exfiltration pair, but still present in default Airbyte workflows.
conditions: IF Airbyte is configured to sync business data from sensitive sources, leakage risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is later granted file or network access, the pair can expose more data classes.
mitigations: Restrict Airbyte connectors to non-sensitive datasets.
Review Airbyte destination settings for outbound transfers.
Keep LlamaFactory offline and without filesystem access.
Separate credentials and service accounts for each agent.
Add a short data-class allowlist before any sync.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress, while LlamaFactory has no write, shell, subprocess, git, or network capabilities. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because the profiles do not describe any orchestrator locking or shared resource management.
conditions: IF both agents are later pointed at the same mutable external API or dataset, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator grants LlamaFactory write or network permissions, reassess overlap.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only and offline.
Avoid giving Airbyte and LlamaFactory the same mutable target.
Use separate service accounts for any shared backend.
Document ownership of each external resource before runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce data outputs, but LlamaFactory has no documented action-taking authority and no input channel is shown that would make it treat Airbyte output as authoritative by default. The cascade is therefore possible only through an external integration not present in the profiles, so the interaction is weakly evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator feeds Airbyte outputs directly into LlamaFactory prompts, cascading error risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is used to generate downstream actions from Airbyte data, reassess severity.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between Airbyte and LlamaFactory.
Require schema validation on Airbyte outputs before reuse.
Do not auto-promote generated text into operational actions.
Log provenance for any data passed from Airbyte to LlamaFactory.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte explicitly touches business data and has broad egress, which can create retention or residency issues if it moves regulated data. LlamaFactory’s profile shows no data classes touched and no network egress, so it is not the primary compliance driver; the risk is mainly Airbyte-side handling of business data in default integrations.
conditions: IF Airbyte processes regulated business data under a residency or retention policy, compliance risk increases.
IF LlamaFactory is later connected to regulated datasets, reassess residency and logging controls.
mitigations: Confirm Airbyte retention settings before syncing.
Limit Airbyte to approved regions and destinations.
Keep LlamaFactory disconnected from regulated datasets.
Record the data class and destination for each Airbyte pipeline.
Review whether any compliance policy applies to outbound transfers.
